meta.title: India Quick Commerce — Market Entry Strategy

slides.title: India Quick Commerce: Winning the Next $12B of Retail
slides.subtitle: Market assessment, unit economics and an 18-month entry play for a new operator

slides.title: Quick commerce will triple by 2028 — but the entry window closes within 18 months

sections.heading: Market
sections.body: GMV grew **8x in three years** to a $5.5B run-rate and is still accelerating: dark-store density passed the convenience tipping point in every metro, and **28M monthly buyers** now default to 10-minute delivery for top-up baskets.

sections.heading: Competition
sections.body: The top three players hold **88% share**, but their playbooks have diverged — only **Blinkit** is contribution-positive at scale, and tier-2 expansion is burning cash across the board, leaving a flank open.

sections.heading: Economics
sections.body: Unit economics flip positive only where order density exceeds **1,100 orders/store/day**. Dense metros pay back a dark store in **14 months**; tier-2 stores may never pay back at current basket sizes.

sections.heading: Recommendation
sections.body: Enter **partner-led**, not greenfield: anchor on an existing retail network, focus on **3 metros**, and buy share where economics already work. The ask is **$150M** for a targeted **12% share** position by 2029.

slides.title: Three playbooks have emerged — and only one is contribution-positive at scale

cells.text: **Premium convenience**: widest catalog, electronics and gourmet mix lift baskets; wins the office-hours and top-up occasions in metros.
**Speed absolutist**: youngest user base, highest order frequency, aggressive city launches — growth bought with the steepest burn of the three.
**Ecosystem player**: rides Swiggy's user base and delivery fleet; capital-efficient expansion but splits management focus across food and grocery.

Entry implication: **concentrate, don't spread** — density in 3 metros beats presence in 15 cities.

slides.title: A partner-led entry beats greenfield on speed and capital — by roughly 2x on both
slides.subtitle: Entry pathway and the four moves that de-risk it

blocks.title: Anchor on existing retail, don't build from zero
blocks.body: A partner's stores, licenses and supplier terms compress launch from 12 months to 5 and cut store capex roughly in half versus greenfield dark stores.

blocks.title: Pilot where the math already works
blocks.body: Launch only in two metros above the 1,100 orders/day density line. Kill gate at month 8: contribution per order must be positive before city three.

blocks.title: Win fresh before anything else
blocks.body: Fresh & dairy is the highest-frequency, worst-served category. Cold-chain investment builds a moat incumbents must re-engineer stores to match.

blocks.title: Copy the AOV lever immediately
blocks.body: Assortment architecture (electronics, gourmet, own-label) lifts baskets without discounting — targeting ₹600+ AOV by month 12.

slides.title: Five initiatives sequence the entry — weighted toward supply-side moats
slides.subtitle: [[accent]]Capital phasing is directional: 60% of the $150M lands in the first 12 months, concentrated on the dark-store network and cold chain that competitors cannot quickly match.[[/]]

principles.text: **Density before breadth** — no city three until cities one and two clear contribution breakeven
Own the **fresh cold chain**; rent everything that isn't a moat
Buy **AOV with assortment**, never with discounts
Every initiative carries a **kill gate** — no zombie spend

goals: **#3 position** by GMV within 24 months of launch
Contribution-positive in **every live metro** by month 18

highlight.title: Recommendation: enter now, partner-led, fresh-first
highlight.body: The market triples by 2028 with or without a new entrant. What closes in 18 months is the ability to enter **cheaply** — every quarter of delay adds dark-store density that must be bought back at greenfield prices. Move on the partner term sheet this quarter.
